toolCallDetails.arguments:
{"path":"snake_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"Create a complete, self-contained classic Snake game in a single HTML file (HTML+CSS+JS all inline, no external dependencies). Requirements:

1. Grid: 30x30 cells, rendered on an HTML5 canvas (each cell e.g. 18px, canvas size 540x540), centered on page with dark theme styling.

2. Game modes selectable from a START MENU (shown on page load, and again after game over until restart):
   - Press "1" = Human vs Human: Snake A controlled by Arrow keys, Snake B controlled by WASD keys.
   - Press "2" = CPU vs Human: Snake A is CPU-controlled, Snake B controlled by Arrow keys (or WASD).
   - Press "3" = CPU vs CPU: both snakes CPU-controlled, fully automatic.
   Menu screen lists the three options with key hints and brief instructions, styled nicely with a title "SNAKE".

3. Two snakes coexist on the grid simultaneously in every mode (each starts at a different position, different color, e.g. green for Snake A, cyan/blue for Snake B). In single-snake conceptual modes, still run two snakes (since only 3 modes are specified: human vs human, cpu vs human, cpu vs cpu — both snakes are always active, controlled per the mode by human keys or CPU AI).

4. Continuous movement: each snake moves automatically every game tick (setInterval or requestAnimationFrame with fixed timestep, ~100-120ms per tick) in its current direction (up/down/left/right) until changed by input or CPU decision. Snake cannot reverse directly into itself (ignore 180-degree reversal input).

5. Growth: one food item (red/yellow dot) spawns randomly on an empty cell; when a snake's head moves onto the food cell, that snake grows by one segment, its score +1, and new food spawns on a random empty cell not occupied by any snake body.

6. Collision / game over conditions per snake: hitting a wall (grid boundary), hitting its own body, or hitting the other snake's body (head or body) ends that snake's run (mark it dead, stop moving it, render it grayed out). When both snakes are dead, OR when only one mode requires ending (see below), show the GAME OVER screen with final scores of both snakes and a message declaring the winner (higher score) or draw. If only one snake dies, keep the other playing until it also dies or optionally end game entirely when the first collision happens (simplest & clearest: game ends immediately when ANY snake collides — show game over screen immediately with both scores and result).

7. CPU AI: for CPU-controlled snake(s), implement pathfinding using BFS (breadth-first search) on the grid from the snake's head to the food, treating snake bodies and walls as obstacles; step the snake in the direction of the first move of the shortest path each tick. If no path exists to the food, fall back to a heuristic: pick the direction (among the 4) that is a legal safe move (doesn't hit wall/self/other snake immediately) and if possible maximizes distance survival (prefer move into open space / greatest available free-neighbor count), avoiding reversing direction.

8. Keyboard controls:
   - Arrow keys = Snake A direction (when Snake A is human-controlled)
   - W/A/S/D = Snake B direction (when Snake B is human-controlled)
   - On start menu: keys "1", "2", "3" select mode and start the game immediately.
   - On game over screen: pressing any key (or specifically Enter/Space) restarts back to the start menu (or directly restarts same mode) — implement: pressing Enter restarts with same mode, pressing Escape or any of 1/2/3 goes back to choose a new mode via the menu overlay.

9. HUD during gameplay: display current score of Snake A and Snake B at the top of the canvas area (e.g. "Snake A: 0   Snake B: 0"), and show which mode is active (e.g. "Mode: CPU vs Human").

10. Structure the file as a single .html document: <!DOCTYPE html> with <style> in <head> for CSS, canvas element in <body>, and <script> at the bottom containing all game logic (Snake class, Food spawning, BFS pathfinding function, game loop, input handlers, rendering, menu/game-over state machine). No external libraries, no network requests, must run by opening the file directly in a browser.

11. Visual polish: dark background (#111 or similar), grid lines optional subtle, distinct bright colors for each snake, food as a distinct color, clean readable font (monospace or sans-serif), centered layout, menu and game-over screens as overlays or full-canvas-replacement text drawn on the canvas itself (not requiring extra DOM elements is fine, but DOM overlay divs are also acceptable if styled well).

12. Code quality: well-organized, commented where helpful, use requestAnimationFrame/setInterval correctly with cleanup on restart (no duplicated intervals), use 'use strict' or clean scoping (IIFE) to avoid global leaks.

Produce the complete final HTML file content now."}
